title: Depth needed for exact ReLU representation of piecewise-linear functions
open_core: Determine the least number of hidden layers with which ReLU networks represent every continuous piecewise-linear function on R^d (equivalently max of d+1 numbers). Hertrich-Basu-Di Summa-Skutella conjectured ceil(log2(d+1)).
status: SOLVED as stated: Bakaev-Brunck-Hertrich-Stade-Yehudayoff (arXiv 2505.14338, STOC'26) disproved the ceil(log2(n+1)) conjecture; Brunck et al. (arXiv 2610.28587v1, Oct 2026, unrefereed) prove every ReLU network is exactly simulated with two hidden layers, so the depth is 2. What is open is size: two hidden layers compute max of N numbers with widths O(N^2) and 2^{O(N log N)} (Zimmermann 2610.26795), and Safran (2601.01417) gives width Omega(d^{1+1/(2^{k-2}-1)}) at depth 3 <= k <= log2 log2 d. Restated problem: is max of n numbers computable exactly by a two-hidden-layer ReLU network of size polynomial in n?  [abstract read on arXiv 2026-11-11, an agent]

title: Implicit bias of sharpness-aware minimization in nonlinear networks
open_core: For a stated two-layer model, characterise the solution selected by SAM with the practical (unnormalised or per-batch) perturbation and compare its generalisation with gradient descent.
status: OPEN: diagonal linear L-layer networks are done (Moon-Si-Yun 2603.08290: l2-SAM reaches the l1 max-margin direction at L = 2, l-infinity-SAM depends on initialisation); scale-invariant two-block problems in Li-Zhang-He 2410.14802. No result found for a nonlinear two-layer model. The row needs a sharp statement (limit direction of l2-SAM on a two-layer homogeneous ReLU network on separable data). title: Which function classes does chain of thought make learnable by gradient descent?
open_core: Give a class learnable by a gradient-trained transformer with intermediate tokens in polynomial samples and not without them, beyond parity, with matching lower bounds.
status: PARTLY DONE: beyond parity, gradient-trained transformers with chain of thought provably learn state tracking with length generalisation (Huang-Wen-Singh-Chi-Chen 2511.07378) and path-finding in trees (Yang-Huang-Liang-Chi 2508.08222). Neither abstract states a lower bound without chain of thought, so the separation with matching lower bounds is open outside parity. Restate with one named task. title: Straightness of iterated rectified flow
open_core: Decide whether iterating the rectification map converges to a straight coupling, and to which one, for general data laws in dimension d >= 2.
status: NARROWED: Pham-Roy-Rinaldo-Sarkar (2610.36090v2) characterise when two-step rectified flow is straight for smooth strongly log-concave densities and Gaussian mixtures and construct non-straight couplings otherwise. So two steps are not always straight. Open: the limit of the k-fold rectification as k grows, for general laws.  [abstract read on arXiv 2026-11-11, an agent]

title: Learning coefficients of nonlinear deep networks
open_core: Compute the real log canonical threshold of the loss at the true parameter for deep ReLU or tanh networks beyond the deep linear case (Aoyagi).
status: OPEN: the deep linear case is done (Aoyagi; Pepin Lehalleur-Rimanyi 2411.19920: threshold C/2 with C the codimension of the fibre); an exact algorithm exists only for two-parameter models (2608.20183). No exact learning coefficient found for deep ReLU or tanh networks.  [abstract read on arXiv 2026-11-11, an agent]

title: The neural feature ansatz for gradient-trained networks
open_core: Prove that the first-layer Gram matrix of a network trained by gradient descent is proportional to a power of the average gradient outer product, in a stated nonlinear model.
status: OPEN: exact analysis found only for linear recursive feature machines (Cheng-Kiani-Lu-Radhakrishnan 2610.09196). One search query only; no proof for a nonlinear gradient-trained network among the hits. The row must name the model.  [abstract read on arXiv 2026-11-11, an agent]

title: Exact power of constant-depth log-precision transformers
open_core: Decide whether such transformers compute all of uniform TC0, or separate them from it.
status: SETTLED WITH PADDING: averaging-hard-attention masked pre-norm transformers with polynomial padding recognise exactly FO-uniform TC0 (Merrill-Sabharwal 2505.18948v2); growing-precision padded transformers reach L-uniform TC0 regardless of width (Svete-Merrill-Cotterell-Sabharwal 2605.30523). Open: the same question without padding. Overlaps agent's H35; keep one row.  [abstract read on arXiv 2026-11-11, an agent]

title: Implicit bias of Adam in homogeneous networks
open_core: Show which margin (l-infinity or other) Adam with standard hyperparameters maximises on separable data for homogeneous nonlinear networks.
status: MOSTLY SETTLED: Gronich-Vardi (2602.16340v3) show Adam without the stability constant converges to KKT points of the l-infinity margin problem on smooth homogeneous models under a decaying learning rate; Gronich-Vardi (2611.01929) show that for constant or weakly decaying schedules (alpha > 1/L - 1/2) Adam has no trajectory-independent margin bias on deep linear networks. What is left (non-smooth ReLU, positive stability constant) is too narrow for a top-200 row.  [abstract read on arXiv 2026-11-11, an agent]
